ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in figure, a uniformly doped Silicon (Si) bar of length \( L = 0.1 \mu m \) with a donor concentration \( N_D = 10^{16} \, \text{cm}^{-3} \) is illuminated at \( x = 0 \) such that electron and hole pairs are generated at the rate of \( G_L = G_{L0}\left(1-\frac{x}{L}\right) \), \( 0 \leq x \leq L \), where \( G_{L0} = 10^{17} \, \text{cm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1} \). Hole lifetime is \( 10^{-4} \, s \), electronic charge \( q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, C \), hole diffusion coefficient \( D_P = 100 \, \text{cm}^2/s \), and low-level injection condition prevails. Assuming a linearly decaying steady-state excess hole concentration that goes to zero at \( x = L \), the magnitude of the diffusion current density at \( x = L/2 \), in \( A/cm^2 \), is ______.
